findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one personal way to reach Mark does nothing when clicked. 'Write to me' has a button's fill and a verb label, and the address is underlined like a link, but the parts map shows both as static. Only the address in the footer, at the very bottom of the page, actually opens an email.
findings.who_objects: The bank official. They read the pitch, decide to get in touch, click the obvious button or the underlined address, and nothing happens. Many will give up or assume the site is broken, which stops the page's one job and undermines trust in a legal advisor.

findings.where: First screen, 'Book a consultation' (a second filled blue button of equal weight to 'Write to me'; links to #consult)
findings.fault: There are two primary buttons of equal weight. The brief asks for one action and one direct personal way to reach Mark, and here the only button that works is the corporate one. 'Book a consultation' promises a booking service that this brochure site does not have, and it points to an in-page anchor rather than to Mark.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief's personal-advisor test calls for one personal contact and no salesy wording. The official, too: they have to choose between two equal buttons, and 'book a consultation' sounds like a law firm's sales funnel, not an independent advisor.

findings.where: First screen, the hero ground: a blue-to-lilac gradient band that stops with a hard edge where the warm paper begins
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pastel blue-to-violet gradient, a colour that is not in the house palette. The page's own palette tile says 'warm paper, grey ink, house blue, three colours, no accent', and the brief asks for a warm paper ground with blue and grey as the only ink. The lilac reads as a generic tech or SaaS landing page, and the band breaks off sharply into the cream page below.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the hero contradicts the brief's palette and the tile's own stated system. The official, because the first impression is a software startup rather than the legal journal this direction promises, which is exactly the techy look the brief rules out.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph 'I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…' (desktop four lines, phone eight lines)
findings.fault: The key sentence saying who Mark serves and what he does is set as a full paragraph of widely spaced bold capitals in the sans. Long runs of capitals are slow to read, and they read as shouting, or as the 'tracked techy capitals' the brief bans. It also goes against the page's own type tile, which keeps the sans for short notes and labels.
findings.who_objects: The official, because this is the sentence that tells them Mark is for them, and it is the hardest text on the screen to read, worst on a phone at eight lines of capitals. The founder, because it breaks the brief's refined, non-techy tone.

findings.where: First screen margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024 with talk titles), and the blue section labels down the left margin (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: These notes are set in the house blue, which the page also uses for links and the action, and the hero notes name specific talks. They look like links to those talks, but they are static (the parts map shows each as 'a link's colour', not acting). The talks are the best proof of Mark's work on the page, yet a visitor cannot open them.
findings.who_objects: The official, who wants to check Mark's record and will click 'Best Practices in PPP Legislation for Emerging Economies' expecting the talk and get nothing. On a site where blue means 'click', this confuses them and hides the evidence they came to weigh.

findings.where: Phone first screens: the contact row at the end of the hero
findings.fault: On a phone the contact row breaks badly. 'Write to me', the address and 'Book a consultation' stack with no space between them, the address touches the button below it, and 'Book a consultation' is indented away from the left edge that everything else keeps. The row also sits near the end of the second phone screen, after the photo and two paragraphs.
findings.who_objects: The official reading on a phone between meetings. The way to reach Mark looks broken and crowded, and it arrives late, so they have to scroll past everything before they find it.

findings.where: Phone first screen, the 'Istanbul, 2025' margin note set between the heading and the photograph
findings.fault: With no margin on a phone, the notes fall in between the blocks. The Istanbul note sits under the large heading as if it were the heading's dateline or the photo's caption, and the Melbourne and São Paulo notes break into the flow of the two paragraphs.
findings.who_objects: The official on a phone, who reads 'Istanbul, 2025' as the source of the headline or the place in the photo. The notes stop working as quiet asides and become clutter, which the brief warns against.

findings.where: First screen photograph and the motion sketch's photograph (both 'exhibit' photos)
findings.fault: Both photos have a wide soft drop shadow, but neither can be acted on, so they look lifted like cards you could click. On the first screen the shadow and the gradient together add to the slick, app-like feel.
findings.who_objects: The founder. The house rule reserves depth for what floats or can be acted on, and the brief asks for restraint, not slick. Few visitors will notice the false lift, but it moves the look away from the 'framed exhibit on paper' idea.

findings.where: Article specimen 'Download' button, compared with the hero buttons
findings.fault: The page uses two button shapes for the same job: square filled buttons in the hero, and a fully rounded outlined pill for 'Download'. Nothing explains the difference.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who has to choose one action style for the site. Few visitors would notice, but the pill looks borrowed from an app kit and is out of place in a legal-journal page.

findings.where: Article specimen heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop)
findings.fault: On desktop the heading breaks at the hyphen, as 'Public-' / 'Private Partnership Law', which splits the key term across two lines.
findings.who_objects: The official, who reads PPP as one term. Polish only, but a journal-style page should not split the term in its own title.
